title: The most unexpected answer to a counting puzzle
beats: Two blocks and a wall; idealize away friction and energy loss, add a clack sound to make the count audible
Equal masses first: three clacks, traced step by step
Mass ratio 100, 10,000, 1,000,000 played in sequence: 31, 314, 3141 clacks; pattern left for viewer
Fake-out: says 313, then 'wait for it', corrects to 314
Names the pattern outright: collisions give digits of pi
Credits viewer and 1995 discoverer; frames it as Olympics of comically inefficient pi algorithms
Absurd four-step algorithm; 20 digits needs a block heavier than a black hole
Over-idealized; not a real algorithm, the interest is why pi appears
Where there is pi there is a hidden circle (energy); answer deferred; asks viewer to try it

metrics.ending: Cliffhanger; hidden circle from energy conservation teased, viewers told to attempt puzzle socially

new_moves.name: promise-then-delay
new_moves.what: Reveal the surprising result fully, explicitly defer the why, and give the viewer homework

new_moves.name: absurd-algorithm-framing
new_moves.what: Recast the phenomenon as a ridiculous procedure to expose scale and deflate hype

theory: The video sells the question, not the answer. A concrete toy world escalates until the pattern forces itself on the viewer, then a deliberate caveat converts 'useless algorithm' into 'why is pi here?'. Withholding the explanation makes curiosity the product.
velocity: Ghost-hands/sim should support escalating runs of the same scene with an audible counter so the learner spots the pattern before it is named
Orchestrator can gate the 'why' behind a learner prediction attempt (ask them to guess before revealing)
Add a deflating-caveat beat to evals: does the tutor say what the demo is NOT
